mechanism_narrative: Sustained weekly increases in WORKPLACES mobility reflect a steady return to office-based routines, which pulls people into central commercial districts and raises associated retail and recreation footfall over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -60.9 to -42.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory for at least two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility exceeding 2 points signals households spending less time confined at home, which translates into increased discretionary outings and higher retail and recreation activity within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped from 39.4 to 32.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after a RESIDENTIAL week-on-week drop exceeding 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active policy-easing regime, a crossing of TRANSIT mobility above the -55 threshold indicates restored public confidence in using transit for non-essential trips, which drives a near-term uptick in retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -55 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -64.6 to -53.9 over the snapshot window
regime_hint: policy easing / lockdown restrictions being lifted
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase in the week following a TRANSIT crossing above -55, or continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility rise together, the combined effect of resumed commuting and transit use compounds to produce a stronger and more persistent increase in retail and recreation mobility than either series would predict alone, over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series rose concurrently from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than what WORKPLACES alone would predict, despite concurrent TRANSIT increases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility during the summer reopening period reflects a seasonal substitution effect where households favor outdoor leisure over indoor retail and recreation venues, causing retail and recreation mobility growth to stagnate or dip over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -61.6 to -56.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at the same or faster pace as PARKS mobility increases over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility decelerates to under 2 points for two consecutive weeks, it signals a plateau in the return-to-office trend, which will stall the recovery momentum of retail and recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change falls below 2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES week-on-week gain slowed from 6.6 points (t-2w to t-1w) to 0.7 points (t-1w to t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC keeps rising in the week following a WORKPLACES deceleration below 2 points for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains comparatively flat while RETAIL_REC mobility rises, it indicates that recovery is being driven by discretionary rather than essential shopping, and this decoupling pattern predicts continued discretionary-led growth in retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change stays within 2 points while RETAIL_REC rises more than 3 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuated narrowly between -13.3 and -18.4 while RETAIL_REC rose from -62.7 to -57.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to continue rising over two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat and RETAIL_REC having recently risen.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of active lockdown easing, a sustained reduction in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with a rise in WORKPLACES mobility jointly indicates policy-driven normalization of daily life, producing a compounded four-week increase in retail and recreation mobility beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while WORKPLACES rises concurrently for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 39.4 to 32.1 while WORKPLACES rose from -60.9 to -42.0 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show accelerated four-week growth beyond single-series predictions despite concurrent RESIDENTIAL decline and WORKPLACES increase.
